r_frame_profile.note: D-330: the stone frames of doors, windows and niches (global.r_door_frame) carved as the doorways of the Achaemenid rock tombs show them (references/Naqsh-e Rustam 3.webp, the tomb door, which copies a palace doorway: B for the tomb): three stepped fasciae nested around the opening over the whole jamb face and the lintel's lower part (on a window or niche also over the sill block, scaled to its height), each stepping back by `step` toward the opening; the lintel crowned by the cavetto (Egyptian gorge) cornice of r_door_frame: a torus roll torus_h high projecting torus_proj at its foot, the hollow gorge flaring out to the cornice projection, a flat fillet fillet_h high on top; the gorge carved with one register of upright round-topped tongues at tongue_pitch, tongue_relief proud (the tomb cornice: one register seen at ~5 cm per px, C; Q-916). Arrises chamfered by `chamfer` and worn (the Blender trim, tools/blender/decor.mjs). Step, torus, fillet and tongue sizes C (by eye from the photograph, scaled to the frame of r_door_frame)

r_window.note: window openings through the wall in monolithic dark-stone frames (Tachara "monolithic door/window/niche frames", WP-EXT C; Hadish 19 windows, IR-PERS B count). Width half the building's main door (C), sill 1.2 m above the floor (C), head level with the door head so lintels and cornices run level (C); frame = r_door_frame jambs, lintel and cornice plus a sill block of sill_block (C). Positions and sizes NOT SEEN (Q-087); no glazing (blocklist glass-windows), no shutters modelled

r_niche.note: blind niches: window-shaped recesses in the inner wall face with the same frame as the windows (Tachara stone frames, WP-EXT C; Hadish 4 niches, IR-PERS B count); depth C (Q-087)

r_door_leaf.note: timber double-leaf doors of the stone-framed palace doorways (C: analogue of the Gate of All Nations, whose pivot sockets show two-leaf doors, WP extract C). Each leaf turns on a vertical post (post_r) standing in a stone socket, its foot shod in bronze (shoe_h; Near Eastern pivot doors, RECOLLECTION); bronze bands across both faces (bands x band_h x band_t; bronze-banded doors are a Neo-Assyrian analogue, RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN for Persepolis) studded with bronze bosses (boss_r at boss_pitch; as gate_nations.r_door_leaves, C). Timber species not known (C). Leaves hang at the inner end of the passage and swing 180 deg through the hall to lie against the inner wall face (the D-032 Gate rule, C; Q-088), so the jamb reliefs on the reveals stay visible. swing_s = time to open or close (1.5 s, C); reach = how far a person can work a leaf from (C). bronze_metalness: the fittings are drawn partly metallic because the renderer has no environment reflection and full metal reads black in shade (the D-030 precedent for gilding, C); boss_range: bosses are drawn on leaves within this distance of the camera (a 22 mm stud is under a pixel beyond it, C)

r_stair_crenellation.note: four-stepped merlons crowning the stair parapets. Motif B on the Apadana stairs (IR-PERS, apadana.r_crenellation); on the Tachara S stair by analogy (tachara.stair_s_reliefs "Persepolis stair convention", C); on the Grand Stair per grand_stair.parapet_height (C); on the Hadish and Tripylon stairs by the same convention (C, NOT SEEN). Size as the Apadana merlon (0.9 x 0.9 m, C), pitch 1.15 x width as on the Apadana (C); depth = the parapet thickness up to max_depth (the Apadana merlon depth, C). Each merlon stands on the lowest parapet block under it (no merlon floats over a lower step; C). The terrace-edge parapet is left plain: terrace.parapet_height assumes crenellations but no source for them was reached (the motif is attested on stairs). The Hadish S balcony "behind four-stepped crenellations" (B) is not modelled (Q-P4 balcony geometry NOT SEEN). D-230: each merlon carries the double-rebated slot of apadana.r_merlon_slot (seen on the Apadana E stair merlons, B; here by the same convention, C).

r_jamb_inscription.note: a door-jamb inscription (XPe on the Hadish E and W doorways: "XPe above king and attendants", SI-ARCH B; "two large Xerxes inscriptions on the eastern and western doorways", FARROKH B): carved on each reveal above the figures, the Old Persian, Elamite and Babylonian versions stacked top to bottom (order C), each version in lines of glyph m signs (C: "large", size NOT SEEN) with line_gap between lines and version_gap between versions, the stack starting top_margin below the reveal top and spanning width_of_reveal of the reveal (C). Whether each reveal carries all three versions or one each is NOT SEEN (Q-090)

r_inscription_carving.note: carved signs are incised into the host stone (D-177): each sign's outline is the edge of a cut whose walls fall at wall_angle_deg to the face (a V-section: the depth at a point is its distance to the sign's edge, deepest in a wedge's head), drawn in the host stone's own material; no measured section or depth was read (Schmidt 1953 NOT SEEN), so the angle and hence the depth are C. The sign quads lie lift m off the face. Several versions or texts in one field share one glyph height, the largest <= the field's glyph_max at which every line of the inscription's own lineation fits and the whole fits the field (never below glyph_min: C); lines gap_ratio x glyph apart; blocks block_sep apart

r_stair_inscription.note: the central-facade inscriptions of the Tachara S stair (XPc) and the Hadish W stair (XPd): trilingual (XPc 'Translations into Elamite and Babylonian', LIVIUS-AI B; XPd 'OP/El/Ak', hadish.stair_w_reliefs B); the three versions stacked between the guards, the Old Persian on top with the Elamite and the Babylonian below it, as the published description of the XPc pillar copies has them ('Translations into Elamite and Babylonian can be seen below the first Old Persian text', LIVIUS-AI B); for this copy the arrangement is C (NOT SEEN). Stacked since D-184: with the edition's own lines (Old Persian and, since D-184, Elamite and Babylonian) three columns side by side did not fit the 2.4 m field at the smallest sign, in the field from the panel top down to bottom_margin above the central ground. Which copies these are (D-177, src/data/royal_inscriptions.json): XPc here is the copy 'on the south wall of the terrace on which the palace is built' (LIVIUS-AI, B; the field C); its copies on the eastern and western pillars of the S portico are NOT carved (no anta face identified in the model, Q-290). XPd here is the copy 'beside the stairs of the Palace of Xerxes' (B; which stair C); its copies on the two pillars of the N portico are NOT carved (Q-290)

r_palace_furnishings.note: palace furnishings (D-212, gap audit item 8). What stood in the halls is NOT attested for Persepolis in 467; the kinds are: throne, footstool, fringed canopy and two incense burners on the Treasury audience reliefs (TREAS-AUD, B); gilded and silver-plated couches, tables of gold and silver and 'gaily coloured' hangings in the establishment Xerxes left to Mardonius (Herodotus 9.80, 9.82: B claim); the knotted-pile carpet of Achaemenid style from Pazyryk kurgan 5, c. 400 BCE, ~1.83 x 2.00 m, red field of squares, borders (PAZYRYK: B for the craft and the size; NOT SEEN this session, recollection); a high couch with a footstool and a table (the Assurbanipal garden relief, ASB-GARDEN: Assyrian analogy); white, green and blue hangings on silver rings (Esther 1:6, ESTHER-1.6: late literary, C). Every size, colour, number and position here is C. With the court absent (the default) the furnishings are rolled, covered and stored and a steward's minimum stays in use; with the court setting on and the court in residence they are laid out for use (C). Lamps are drawn unlit (the torches and braziers of the fire system light the halls)

r_masons_marks.note: masons' and sculptors' marks (D-212, gap audit item 13). Attested: hundreds of sculptors' marks incised on the BACKGROUNDS of the Persepolis reliefs, each the mark of a sculptor or team labelling a figure or a group, e.g. the 'double diamond' mark in front of the spear blade of one archer and above the quiver of another (ROAF1983, search extract: B); marks on blocks at Persepolis and Susa that resemble Lydian letters (IR-GREECE7, MATCULT-R: B); at Pasargadae circles, crosses and L-shaped signs, as on the Lydian palace terraces at Sardis (PAS-MARKS, search extract: B). Only these four shapes are cut: the double lozenge (its exact form NOT SEEN: two lozenges joined point to point, C) and the circle, cross and L of Pasargadae (their use at Persepolis C). Which figure carries which mark, the size (5 cm on the reliefs, 9 cm on the drums), the stroke and the placement on the dressed drums' upper bedding faces are C. Incised as the inscriptions are (V-section, walls at 45 deg, D-177)

r_masonry.note: D-232: the joint layout of the Terrace retaining walls, measured on photograph #24 rectified onto the wall planes with the solved camera of D-230 (tools/dev/masonry_photo_d232.py; the joints read by eye on 4-5x crops with a 0.5 m grid, checked against an automatic bed profile). Courses laid level: 47 course heights, median 1.10 m (IQR 0.90-1.35, 0.45-1.65; 21 % thinner than 0.75 m, 15 % 1.5 m or more), drawn from their deciles (course_q), quantised to 2 cm; one course table per wall section (a face's plane picks one of 4) and one for the Grand Stair recess. Blocks: 57 lengths, median 2.2 m (IQR 2.0-3.5, 1.15-7.0; 26 % 3.5 m or more): drawn as runs of 4 cells of 1.9 m whose 3 inner joints are present with p 0.6, jittered +-0.25 cell (p25/median/p75 1.77/2.13/3.6, 27 % >= 3.5 m, max 7.6: CPU mirror, tests/masonry_d232.test.ts). A block of a course >= 1.4 m is split in a thin and a thick piece in 25 % (the photo's 0.46 + 1.1 m pieces of its 1.6 m course over ~22 % of its length, read the other way as blocks spanning two thin courses). The foot: large irregular blocks and dressed bedrock (IR-PERS: the Terrace partly cut from the rock, B) along 38 % of the 203 m of W wall read, 4.9 m high where present (median 4.84, IQR 4.74-5.29 above the plain at -11.8), 15 % of the wall area; its blocks 3.5-6.8 m long (median 5.8) by 1.4-2.2 m (median 1.8): a row-jittered Voronoi of 4.6 x 1.8 m cells, present on W- and S-facing walls where a 110 m plan noise exceeds theta (placed to agree with #24: present on the salient's W face for its first ~62 m, absent S of it), joints 4 mm with 2 cm rounded arrises, faces tilted up to +-1.5 deg (rougher than the dressed ashlar: C; the ruin's open joints are weathering). Grand Stair recess walls (#33, by eye: blocks of irregular height with jogged beds and leaning head joints, the IR-PERS 'huge irregular blocks', B): the same courses, split share 0.5 at 0.25-0.75 of the height, head joints leaning up to +-12 deg (C). Joint width of the dressed ashlar unchanged (Q-071). Not modelled: the foot's stepped-back plinth (geometry), Q-600
